title: Grateful Dead Live at Tivoli Theater on 1972-04-14

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a blazing April‑14 1972 Europe show – pedal‑steel Looks Like Rain, soaring Dark Star and monster Good Lovin’/Caution make it legendary.
ai_review.review: The recording is an almost flawless SBD that delivers crystal‑clear guitars, Keith’s piano wizardry and the rare Jerry pedal‑steel on “Looks Like Rain.” The performance is high‑octane from start to finish – a fiery first set capped by a monster Dark Star that flows into a thunderous second set of Truckin’, Sugar Magnolia and an unstoppable Good Lovin’/Caution stretch. Minor mix quirks (a low steel level in the rain segment) and track‑splitting complaints don’t dent the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews uniformly rate the show 5 stars, praising both musical firepower and pristine soundboard quality; only minor mix or track‑split issues are noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced SBD with superb clarity on guitars, piano and vocals. A few reviewers note the pedal‑steel being slightly low in the mix during “Looks Like Rain” and occasional track‑split complaints, but overall the audio is pristine.

poor_songs: Cumberland (a bit flat in this mix)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong momentum with Bertha, Brown Eyed Women and a soaring Dark Star; second set peaks with Truckin', a soulful Sugar Magnolia segue and the epic Good Lovin'/Caution jam, delivering a seamless arc of energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Rare pedal‑steel on “Looks Like Rain” shines; his guitar tone and soloing are described as soaring, magical and occasionally buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass praised for sweet harmony vocals, punchy riffs and dominant moments (especially during Dark Star and the Feelin’ Groovy teases).
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar and vocal contributions noted; his banter and solid comping keep the band tight throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano is called “magical,” “articulate monster,” and a driving force that dominates many tracks, especially in the Dark Star and Truckin' sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann lauded as underrated, providing a perfect canvas with funky fills and powerful cymbal work; no specific mention of Mickey.
